source_discovery_run.digest_semantics_note: The discovery run manifest records the uncompressed JSON payload SHA-256 under artifact_digests, whereas GitHub Actions metadata reports the ZIP artifact digest. Both are preserved separately.

rules: Every record remains a candidate until human review.
Similarity does not imply historical descent, common origin, or diffusion.
Publication and index dates are preserved separately; indexing novelty is not publication novelty.
Human remains and mortuary contexts require cultural-sensitivity review.
Biomedical or psychiatric correlation is not evidence of historical religious meaning, neurodivergence, diagnosis, or identity.
Observed practice is not equivalent to explicit propositional belief.

new_candidates.title: Acting under uncertainty: Prediction, contingency, and the function of magic
new_candidates.candidate_relevance: Proposes a bio-cultural model in which magical ritual applies high-level explanatory priors to uncertain or opaque contingency events and may coordinate responses across family/community social levels.
new_candidates.epistemic_caution: Theoretical model only. It does not establish the function of any particular archaeological or historical practice.

new_candidates.title: Coherence and the memorability of supernatural concepts
new_candidates.candidate_relevance: Two studies suggest recall effects may be driven by conceptual coherence rather than simply the number of ontological violations, pressuring minimally-counterintuitive accounts.
new_candidates.epistemic_caution: Laboratory recall mechanisms do not establish historical transmission, origin, prevalence, or meaning.

new_candidates.title: The many manifestations of magical thinking: a systematic review
new_candidates.candidate_relevance: Review of 191 studies finds magical thinking across clinical and non-clinical populations and cultural contexts, providing a strong guard against pathologizing magical or supernatural ideas by themselves.
new_candidates.epistemic_caution: Do not retroactively diagnose historical people, accused witches, ritual specialists, shamans or archaeological populations from cultural resemblance.

new_candidates.title: Religious Alief
new_candidates.candidate_relevance: Develops religious alief as an analytical category for automatic or habitual states that influence behavior without explicit or tacit propositional belief, directly relevant to NOEMA's practice-versus-belief ontology.
new_candidates.epistemic_caution: A philosophical analytical proposal, not an observed mental state in historical actors.

new_candidates.title: Żórawina prehistoric burial mound with 42-tooth necklace and additional skull remains
new_candidates.candidate_relevance: A burial mound near Żórawina contained an adult male, a necklace of 42 drilled teeth, stone/flint implements and remains from two additional human skulls. Planned radiocarbon, DNA and species analyses could materially change interpretation.
new_candidates.epistemic_caution: The date shortly before 2900 BCE is preliminary; radiocarbon is pending. Tooth species, relation of the skulls, and warrior/leader/ritual/decapitation interpretations remain unresolved.

candidate_updates.finding: Analysis of 822 supernatural explanations from 114 historical societies reports moralistic explanations across social scales and varied agents, including minor spirits, witches, shamans/ritual specialists, superior gods and high gods.
candidate_updates.action: Review agent type, reward/punishment, moral content and social scale as separate dimensions; do not collapse agent categories or infer historical descent.

candidate_updates.action: Review for practice-specific neural correlates while keeping neural correlation, phenomenology, theology, clinical outcome and historical interpretation separate.
